QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_57

question.text: What is 'inter-commodity spread' trading in futures markets?

answer.text: Going long futures on one commodity and short futures on another economically related commodity — examples include gold/silver, guar seed/guar gum, or soybean/soya oil
Trading the same commodity on two different exchanges simultaneously
Buying and selling the same futures contract within the same trading day
Converting a futures position from one asset class to another

explanation.text: The Logic: Series XVI (pp.105-106) defines an inter-commodity spread as taking a long position in futures on one commodity and an offsetting short position in futures on a different but economically related commodity. The profit comes from changes in the relative price relationship rather than the absolute level. The Trap: An index-versus-index trade such as NIFTY versus Bank NIFTY is not an inter-commodity spread — it is an inter-product/pairs trade, and Series VIII p.55 notes that only calendar spreads are available in the equity derivatives segment. Trading on two exchanges is inter-exchange arbitrage; intra-day buy/sell is day trading; switching asset classes is a position change, not a spread. Note: Source-backed by Series VIII p.55 and Series XVI pp.105-106.
